title: Staggered maintenance credits + SQ extraction pilot for private/VPC packaging
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers deploying Redwood Private/VPC repeatedly ask for clearer, simpler upgrade/maintenance economics and faster security questionnaire (SQ) turnarounds. Current proposals bundle license fees, support tiers, and upgrade cadence in lengthy contracts; Security/Legal teams manually fill much of the SQ leading to multi-week delays for procurement.

Goal: Run a pricing and packaging experiment that tests (A) a staggered maintenance-credit model (maintenance credits replace fixed annual upgrade fees and give customers a consumable credit pool for upgrades/patch windows), (B) three support tiers with explicit included maintenance credits and SLAs, and (C) an automated SQ-extraction pipeline that pre-populates common fields to reduce turnaround time. Evaluate revenue neutrality and procurement speed for 3 pilot customers.

Proposed packaging (pilot matrix):
- Band A (Small footprint): one-time license fee = $75k, includes 100 maintenance credits /yr, Standard support (8x5 response, 48h P1), upgrade cadence: quarterly minor, annual major (can use credits for out-of-band patch windows).
- Band B (Mid footprint): one-time license fee = $250k, includes 350 maintenance credits /yr, Priority support (24x7 P1, 4h initial), upgrade cadence: monthly minor, semi-annual major (credits provide expedited windowing or emergency patches).
- Band C (High footprint / regulated): one-time license fee = $750k, includes 1,200 maintenance credits /yr, Enterprise support (dedicated TAM + 2h P1, scheduled major upgrades with blackout windows), upgrade cadence: continuous rolling with scheduled maintenance windows; credits extend maintenance SLAs.

How credits work: Maintenance credits are consumed when Redwood performs non-standard upgrades, emergency security patches, or out-of-band on-prem maintenance that requires scheduling customer ops time. Credits regenerate annually; customers can purchase top-ups. This creates a predictable contracted fee (license + expected support uplift) while allowing variability for real operational work.

SQ automation: Build a lightweight extraction pipeline that ingests customer SQ PDFs/word templates and pre-fills 70-90% of frequent items (hosting environment, data residency, encryption-in-transit/at-rest flags, auditing controls, KMS footprint). Outputs a pre-filled SQ bundle for Legal review. Start with most common frameworks used by pilot customers (SIG, Cloud-specific vendor SQs).

Pilot customers: ACME Labs (mid), FinOptima (regulated), NovaRetail (small). Targeted pilot contract signings: 3 signed pilots by 2025-04-15.

Decision levers: price bands, credits-per-band, support SLA deltas, SQ automation coverage thresholds and confidence. Finance will validate revenue neutrality scenarios (LTV/CAC impact) before scaling.

Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: Customers see credits as unpredictable spend. Mitigation: Provide credit burn dashboards in Console and a predictable credit-to-cost mapping.
- Risk: SQ automation introduces incorrect answers. Mitigation: Always require Legal sign-off and surface confidence scores on prefilled items.
- Risk: Operational load for manual top-ups/patches. Mitigation: Pilot limits top-up purchases via playbook and include support engineering on-call budget for pilot duration.

Outcome: Recommend one of three go/no-go outcomes at pilot completion: Adopt (scale packaging + add to quote generator), Iterate (change bands/credits and re-run with second cohort), or Abandon (revert to existing licensing model).
acceptance_criteria: 3 pilot customers signed pilot contracts using the new bands and credit model
SQ extraction pipeline reduces manual SQ prep time by >= 50% (baseline measured) and achieves >= 85% auto-fill accuracy on common fields
Billing integration captures maintenance credit top-ups and consumption events in billing ledger with reconciliation for pilot customers
Console shows credit balance and predicted burn for pilot customers
Legal and Security sign-off on SQ automation approach and playbook
Pilot retrospection doc with recommendation and financial sensitivity analysis completed
metrics: Pilot ARR delta vs baseline pricing (target: revenue-neutral to +10%)
Maintenance credit utilization rate (target: 25-60% of included credits)
Upgrade success rate (target: >= 98% for scheduled windows)
